reference.notes:
`basename` now skips trailing separators and returns the last non-empty segment of the path, as the spec describes. All tests pass: the 38 in the visible suite, the 31 in the hidden suite, and the full run of 381. ESLint, Prettier and `tsc --noEmit` also report no problems.

**What changed:** `src/path.ts` had no `not implemented` stubs. It already had working `basename` and `parse` code, and the doc comments on them were already in the working tree. I changed only the body of `basename` (`src/path.ts:257`). It now splits `normalizeWindowsPath(p)` on `/` and walks back to the last non-empty segment, returning `""` if there isn't one. That means:
- A run of trailing `/` and `\` in any mix is skipped.
- Empty segments in the middle of a path don't matter.
- `.` and `..` come back as they are.
- Paths with no segment at all, like `/` or `\\`, return `""`.
- Drive-only paths like `C:\` return `C:`.

The extension is still removed the same way as before, so it is matched against the segment after the trailing separators are gone. `parse` picks up the fix through `basename`, and no other function changed.
